# The division of Daniel into reading units: a record of what was disputed

This record is generated mechanically from the reports of the readers who examined a proposed division of the book of Daniel into 75 reading units. It is written for a reader of Daniel, not for a reader of the project that produced it: passages are named by chapter and verse, in the English numbering, with the Hebrew numbering added where the two differ.

Every quotation set off with a rule at the left is a reader's own sentence, altered only by the mechanical substitutions listed in full near the end. Every other sentence is the generator's own frame, and every such sentence is printed in the last section so that the frame can be inspected apart from the evidence.

This record makes no judgement of its own. It changes no unit, weighs no boundary and settles no dispute; it reports what the readers wrote. Its limits are stated in section 2 and are not small.

## 1. What made this book difficult

Daniel is written in two languages. Of the 75 units, 30 lie in Hebrew, 44 in Aramaic and 1 cross from one to the other (Daniel 2:1–4). The formula inventory counts 357 verses in 12 chapters.

The Hebrew and English traditions number the verses differently in four stretches, so that a boundary stated in one numbering can be misread in the other. The section-mark layer states the difference in these words:

> MT != WEB in two zones (MT 3:31-33 = WEB 4:1-3 and MT 4:1-34 = WEB 4:4-37; MT 6:1 = WEB 5:31 and MT 6:2-29 = WEB 6:1-28); identity in every other chapter. Byte-proven in a working file. EVERY ref in this file is MT.

The Hebrew text carries paragraph marks, and the division had to decide how much weight each bears. The section-mark layer holds 30 marked verses: 22 PE, 8 SAMEKH.

> SAMEKH = setumah (closed section), PE = petuchah (open section), recorded on the verse the mark FOLLOWS. Masoretic paragraph evidence: it informs a boundary and never decides one alone, and translation formatting never drives a boundary at all (a logged error).

The book marks time with date notices and recurring formulae, and several of the disputes below turn on whether a formula opens a unit or merely continues one. The formula inventory records 8 date notices and the following formulae:

The division as it stands is not confident. Its own grades of confidence are: low, 2; medium, 26; medium-low, 47. Its unit types are: dialogue, 10; doxology or prayer, 4; dream or vision report, 9; heavenly discourse, 13; interpretation, 8; narrative, 22; royal proclamation, 3; summary notice, 6.

## 2. How the division was examined, and what that does and does not establish

The division was read in stages. Two first readings, here called reading A and reading B, each examined every unit without sight of the other (22 reports, 150 findings). A reconciling reading then took both and said which stood (6 reports, 75 findings). The entries were revised in rounds (19 revision logs opened here, with 311 recorded changes), and the later revisions were re-read in pairs, one reading attending to scope and one to the text (10 reports). An audit followed (1 report and 1 supplement). An adjudicator ruled between the stages (12 rounds, 116 rulings).

What this does not establish. Every reading at every stage was produced by one family of language model. Where two readings agree, that is one voice heard twice, not two independent witnesses, and agreement in this record must never be taken as confirmation. No human scholar has examined any unit. No reading consulted a version, a manuscript or a commentary beyond the two witnesses named in section 8. The readers said as much themselves; their own statements of limit are collected in section 6.

Of the 141 files the project lists as landed, 59 were opened and quoted, 58 were opened and checked but not quoted, and 24 were not opened (20 closing messages and 4 revision logs held outside the tree). Section 7 lists every one.

## 3. The disputes

A passage appears here if either first reading challenged its entry, if the first readings differed, if a later re-reading challenged it or added a finding on it, or if the audit recorded a finding on it. 64 of the 75 units appear. They are ordered by the highest severity any reader assigned, then by their place in the book. Severity is the readers' own grade; most challenges concern how an entry words or supports its boundary, not where the boundary falls.

By highest severity: high, 1; medium, 16; low, 47.

### Daniel 10:15–19 — highest severity: high

The unit as it stands: language Hebrew; type dialogue; confidence medium-low.

The stated reason for the boundary, as the entry now reads:

(the entry's own words)

> Onset: 10:15 (Hebrew numbering) resumes after the speech with וּבְדַבְּר֣וֹ עִמִּ֔י (OSHB/WLC) and the seer setting his face to the ground, נָתַ֧תִּי פָנַ֛י אַ֖רְצָה (OSHB/WLC; the set-face formula). Behind it, 10:14 closes the opening speech. Inside the unit Daniel answers (10:16-10:17) and is touched and addressed again (10:18-10:19). Close: 10:19 (Hebrew numbering) ends with the seer's consent, וָאֹֽמְרָ֛ה יְדַבֵּ֥ר אֲדֹנִ֖י כִּ֥י חִזַּקְתָּֽנִי (OSHB/WLC), let my lord speak. Across that edge, 10:20 (Hebrew numbering) opens וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הֲיָדַ֨עְתָּ֙ לָמָּה בָּ֣אתִי אֵלֶ֔יךָ (OSHB/WLC), 10:20 (English numbering) “Do you know why I have come to you?” (WEB), a new question that frames what follows. The close is two-sided but rests on a speech-onset formula for the same messenger, so it is held low (interpretive).

The strongest alternative the entry considered and declined:

> A cut at 10:17/10:18, where 10:18 (Hebrew numbering) has וַיֹּ֧סֶף וַיִּגַּע בִּ֛י (OSHB/WLC), a further touch, was weighed. It was declined because 10:18-10:19 answers the weakness Daniel voices in 10:16-10:17, so the exchange would be split between complaint and reply (interpretive); it would also leave a two-verse remainder.

**Evidence on each side.**

Reading A: verdict challenge; severity high; its proposed course:

> reword the formula notes

Its claim:

> the formula notes states, under the evidence grade read from the source, that the translation at 10:19 gives the greeting and stops, and that the Hebrew clause in which Daniel is strengthened and asks his lord to speak has no English counterpart. That is false. The WEB witness carries the second half of 10:19 on a continuation line after a paragraph break inside the verse. The evidence grade is stronger than the evidence and the layer holds the opposite fact. The boundary itself is unaffected: the close at 10:19 is the seer's request, on both faces.

The two sides as it set them out:

> Onset 10:14/10:15: the first speech is over; 10:15 resumes and the seer goes mute. Close 10:19/10:20: 10:19 ends with the seer's request that his lord speak; 10:20 answers with a question that frames the long speech. The close joins a request to its answer, so it is two-sided but soft, and medium-low stands. No cut is proposed.

The evidence it cited:

> the English text, chapter 10: the line for verse 19 reads 10:19 (English numbering) “Greatly beloved man, don’t be afraid. Peace be to you. Be strong. Yes, be strong.” after 'He said,'; the NEXT line, a paragraph line with no verse number and before verse 20, reads 10:19 (English numbering) “When he spoke to me, I was strengthened, and said,” followed by the request to let his lord speak (read from the source; printed by work script s4)

> the Hebrew-Aramaic text 10:19, words 9 to 15: וַחֲזָ֑ק וּֽבְדַבְּר֤וֹ עִמִּי֙ הִתְחַזַּ֔קְתִּי וָאֹֽמְרָ֛ה יְדַבֵּ֥ר אֲדֹנִ֖י (OSHB/WLC), the clause the entry quotes; the WEB continuation line is its rendering

> device inventory web format: 76 continuation lines in 40 verses, and its note says the clean file has one verse line per verse plus poetry and paragraph continuation lines (read from the source); the entry read only the verse line

> the rest of the entry holds: the formula “'I/he set (my/his) face' (Hebrew)” 10:15, the formula “'and behold' (Hebrew)” 10:16, the formula “the vision/appearance noun מראה, any form (Hebrew; substring)” 10:16 and 10.18, the formula “'fear not' (Hebrew)” and the formula “'and he said' (Hebrew)” 10:19 are all in the inventory; the mark layer's other-notes list has one untyped note at 10:19 saying one or more consonants are read differently from BHS, and no K/Q, paseq, PE or SAMEKH entry for 10:15-10.19 (counted work script s4)

> all Hebrew and WEB quotations in the entry are exact substrings at their cited verses (counted work script s5)

> the unit type dialogue fits (the seer speaks at 10:16-10:17 and 10:19, the figure at 10:19), and the rival at 10:17/10:18 is the strongest interior one

The correction it suggested:

> the translation does render the second half of 10:19: after a paragraph break inside the verse it has Daniel strengthened and asking his lord to speak, so the close can be cited from both faces and no gap in the English is to be reported

> 10:19

Reading B: verdict challenge; severity high; its proposed course:

> reword the formula notes

Its claim:

> The entry states under an read from the source evidence grade that the WEB text at 10:19 stops after the greeting and has no English counterpart for the Hebrew closing clause. That is false on the WEB bytes: verse 10:19 has a second line that renders the clause, the counterpart of the Hebrew the entry quotes.

The two sides as it set them out:

> No cut proposed; the edge at 10:19/10:20 does not move. Near side: 10:19 ends with the seer's consent in both witnesses. Far side: 10:20 opens with a speech formula and the messenger's question. The entry's own weighing (held low, same speaker) stands.

The evidence it cited:

> WEB 10:19, second line of the verse in the pinned WEB file: “Let my lord speak, for you have strengthened me.” (10:19 (English numbering))

> 10:19 (Hebrew numbering) closing five words וָאֹֽמְרָ֛ה יְדַבֵּ֥ר אֲדֹנִ֖י כִּ֥י חִזַּקְתָּֽנִי (copied from the witness line), the splice the entry quotes

> the WEB file prints 10:19 as a verse line plus one continuation line; reading the verse line alone shows only the greeting, which is the likely cause (interpretive)

> mark layer notes other at 10:19: one untyped note, that one or more consonants are read differently from BHS; the K/Q layer has no entry at 10:19 - both statements of the entry about the note are true

> programmatic collation of the entry: every Hebrew run found as an exact substring of the witness line at its cited oshb reference; every curly-quoted WEB string found verbatim on a line of its cited WEB verse (Hebrew at 10:15 twice, 10:18, 10:19, 10:20; WEB at 10:20)

> mark layer (WLC/OSHB, single witness), Dan 9:27-11:21: paragraph marks only PE after 9:27, 10:3 and 10:21; paseq entries in 10:1-11:20 only at 10:12, 10:13, 11:14, 11:17, 11:18 (one each); K/Q sites in 10:1-11:20 only at 11:10 (three), 11:12 (one), 11:18 (one); one untyped editorial note at 10:19

> device layer: the formula “'I/he set (my/his) face' (Hebrew)” 10:15; the formula “'and behold' (Hebrew)” 10:16; the formula “the vision/appearance noun מראה, any form (Hebrew; substring)” 10:16, 10:18; the formula “'fear not' (Hebrew)” 10:19; the formula “'and he said' (Hebrew)” 10:19

> secondary consequence: the rationale gives the close at 10:19 no WEB quotation; with the false note removed the gloss can match the splice

The correction it suggested:

> WEB 10:19 renders the closing clause on a continuation line after a paragraph sign, so the close can be cited from both witnesses; the statement that the English lacks it goes

> WEB 10:19 with 10:19 (Hebrew numbering)

The first readings did not disagree here.

**Resolution.**

The reconciling reading said which reading stands:

> The entry's span 10:15-10:19 stands; the high finding both readings raised was right on the earlier entry and is cured.

Its reason, from the text:

> The pinned WEB of 10:19 has the greeting and then, on a continuation line of the same verse, the clause in which the seer is strengthened and answers; the earlier entry said the WEB stopped after the greeting, under read from the source, and that was false. 10:19 (Hebrew numbering) has 17 words with the atnah on word 9; words 10-17 are the strengthening clause and the reply, which is the range the current the formula notes gives. The entry now reads the close from both witnesses. The readings had described the clause by different word ranges; the count on the bytes is 10-17. The mark layer carries one other note at 10:19 and no K/Q. The close 10:19/10:20 has no section mark; it rests on the completed strengthening before the messenger's new speech at 10:20, a reading graded medium-low. The readings agreed here and the agreement is confirmed on the bytes.

It held the finding of reading A (severity high) to be cured, on this basis:

> the adjudication on Daniel 10:15–19 adopted the finding; the false statement is gone from the formula notes and the close is stated from both witnesses with the word range the bytes give.

It held the finding of reading B (severity high) to be cured, on this basis:

> Same finding, same cure under the adjudication on Daniel 10:15–19 and a numbered adjudication item.

The adjudicator, in round 6, ruled (adopt):

> The high finding is confirmed on the bytes. The false statement about the WEB at 10:19 is removed.

> The entry says the WEB renders the greeting and stops and that the Hebrew closing clause has no English counterpart, and evidence grades this read from the source. The pinned WEB carries the clause in full on a continuation line of the same verse. The statement is false on a pinned file under the strongest evidence grade word.

The audit's verdict on the entry: confirm.

Its reason:

> Daniel 10:15–19 (10:15-10:19): oshb 10:19 has 17 words and words 10 to 17 are the strengthening clause the entry quotes (measured); the note at 10:19 is in the mark layer; no section mark at either seam.

Recorded changes to this entry across all revision rounds: 1.

### Daniel 3:24–27 — highest severity: medium

The unit as it stands: language Aramaic; type narrative; confidence medium-low.

The stated reason for the boundary, as the entry now reads:

(the entry's own words)

> Onset: 3:24 has the king astonished and questioning his counselors; behind the edge, a PE (single-witness) follows 3:23, the verse of the fall into the furnace (read from the source, OSHB mark layer). The opener then is weak, so the onset leans on the PE and the change of focus (interpretive). Close: 3:27 has the assembled officials see that 3:27 (English numbering) “the fire had no power on their bodies”, a witness report that seals the rescue. Across the edge, 3:28 moves from narration to royal speech with the blessing formula (the formula “'blessed/bless' (Aramaic); ברך is also 'knelt' - see the homograph note”); it opens with the answered-and-said formula (read from the source, device inventory), which is weak by itself (interpretive). Inside the span a SAMEKH (single-witness) follows 3:25, between the sight of four men and the call to come out (read from the source, OSHB mark layer); it is weighed as a rival and not taken.

The strongest alternative the entry considered and declined:

> A cut at 3:25/3:26 on the SAMEKH, giving two entries of two verses each, 3:24-25 and 3:26-27 (counted, WEB). Declined: 3:26 opens with then, a weak connective, and the call to come out answers the sight of 3:25 within one scene; a SAMEKH does not decide a seam on its own (interpretive).

**Evidence on each side.**

Reading A: verdict challenge; severity low; its proposed course:

> reword the stated reason for the boundary

Its claim:

> 3:24-3:27 (the king's astonishment, the four in the fire, the call to come out, the officials' inspection) is one movement of discovery and public witness, and its edges are honestly graded. The defect: the stated reason for the boundary and the strongest alternative considered carry no evidence grade word although they hold mark claims (PE after 3:23, SAMEKH after 3:25), device claims (the blessing formula at 3:28; the weak opener at 3:26) and a count (two entries of two verses).

The two sides as it set them out:

> No cut proposed. Onset 3:23/3:24 is weighed under the preceding entry. Close 3:27/3:28: 3:27 is narration, the officials seeing the unharmed men, which completes the rescue; 3:28 changes to the king's speech and carries the blessing. Interior 3:25/3:26: a SAMEKH follows 3:25, but 3:26 opens with a weak connective and the call to come out depends on the sight of 3:25, so the mark alone makes no edge.

The evidence it cited:

> evidence grade-word count per prose field, by my read-only script over the pinned entries: Daniel 3:24–27 the stated reason for the boundary 0, the strongest alternative considered 0, the formula notes 4

> mark layer: PE after 3:23, SAMEKH after 3:25; K/Q at 3:25 and 3:26, both disclosed; none at 3:24 or 3:27

> device inventory: the formula “'then' באדין / אדין (Aramaic)” at 3:24 and 3:26; the formula “'answered ... and said' (Aramaic; up to five words between)” at 3:24, 3:25 and 3:26; the formula “'the Most High' (Aramaic)” at 3:26; the formula “'blessed/bless' (Aramaic); ברך is also 'knelt' - see the homograph note” at 3:28; the listed signals hold with no further hit in 3:24-3:27

> the 3:27 (English numbering) and 3:25 (English numbering) quotations are verbatim; the three Aramaic slices are exact substrings at 3:24 and 3:25 (programmatic test)

> the divided reading at 3:25 is reported neutrally with reported evidence grades and bears on no seam

> form: the unit type narrative fits (short speeches inside narration, sealed by a narrated witness report); confidence medium-low stands; the cut on the SAMEKH at 3:25/3:26 is the strongest interior rival

The correction it suggested:

> the PE after 3:23 and the SAMEKH after 3:25 are single-witness mark-layer facts, the blessing formula at 3:28 and the weak opener of 3:26 are device-inventory facts, 3:24-3:25 and 3:26-3:27 are two verses each by count, and the dependence of the call on the sight is a reading

> 3:23, 3:25, 3:26, 3:28

Reading B: verdict challenge; severity low; its proposed course:

> reword the stated reason for the boundary

Its claim:

> The mark facts are true (PE after 3:23, SAMEKH after 3:25) and the inner SAMEKH is disclosed and weighed, but the stated reason for the boundary and the strongest alternative considered carry no evidence grade word for them. One extent point in the formula notes: the WEB words quoted for the two-word Aramaic splice at 3:25 begin with 'like', which renders the participle standing before the splice, so the WEB quotation reaches one Aramaic word further back than the splice.

The two sides as it set them out:

> Onset side: a PE follows 3:23; 3:24 opens with the weak connective and the king's astonishment. Close side: 3:27 is the officials' witness and no mark follows it; 3:28 opens with the answer formula and the blessing, a change from narration to royal speech. Inside, the SAMEKH after 3:25 is followed by 3:26 opening with the weak connective. The onset leans on the PE and the close on the change of voice, as the entry says; medium-low stands.

The evidence it cited:

> the stated reason for the boundary: 'a PE (single-witness) follows 3:23' and 'a SAMEKH (single-witness) follows 3:25' have no evidence grade word; the strongest alternative considered: the SAMEKH and the count 'two entries of two verses' have no evidence grade word

> extent: the word before the splice at 3:25 (Hebrew numbering), copied from the verse line, is דָּמֵ֖ה ; the WEB 'like' answers to it together with the preposition prefixed to the splice

> SUPPORTED: both splices are exact substrings at 3:25 (Hebrew numbering) and 3:24 (Hebrew numbering); the ketiv/qere note of 3:25 is on a different word (the ordinal), as the entry says, and 3:24 carries none; the plural form of the second splice word matches the WEB plural; WEB quotations at 3:27 (English numbering) and 3:25 (English numbering) verbatim; ketiv/qere at 3:25 (1) and 3:26 (1) is the complete set for 3:24-27; no paseq in the span; 3:26 (Hebrew numbering) opens with the connective

> ketiv/qere layer, MT 3:1-33, verses and note counts: 3:3(1) 3:5(1) 3:7(1) 3:10(3) 3:12(2) 3:15(1) 3:18(2) 3:19(1) 3:21(1) 3:25(1) 3:26(1) 3:28(1) 3:29(1) 3:31(1) 3:32(1); no other verse of the chapter; paseq verses in the chapter: 3:2 and 3:15 only

> The PE after 3:23 and the SAMEKH after 3:25 are extracted single-witness facts of the WLC mark layer; the WEB phrase for the fourth figure renders the participle together with the two-word phrase

> 3:23 (Hebrew numbering); 3:25 (Hebrew numbering); 3:25 (English numbering)

The first readings did not disagree here.

**Resolution.**

The reconciling reading said which reading stands:

> The entry's span web 3:24-27 stands at its lowered grade; both readings kept the span.

Its reason, from the text:

> A PE follows oshb 3.23. A SAMEKH follows 3.25 inside the span, and the entry weighs it as a rival and declines it because the formula “'then' באדין / אדין (Aramaic)” heads 3.26. The answer formula and the formula “'blessed/bless' (Aramaic); ברך is also 'knelt' - see the homograph note” are listed at 3.28 on the far side. The spliced phrase is words 20-21 of oshb 3.25; the WEB wording the entry quotes also renders the sense of word 19.

It held the finding of reading A (severity low) to be cured, on this basis:

> adjudication round 6 a numbered adjudication item and adjudication round 8 a numbered adjudication item: five annotations in the rationale, none off the grammar.

No five-word WEB run stands in the field outside the quotation convention.

### Limits the readers stated themselves

Each reader was required to say what it could not establish. Those statements follow, grouped by stage, each with the reader's own account of why it matters. Repeated statements are printed once.

**First readings.**

> All thirteen pinned inputs were hashed and matched. The toolkit note and the set of automated checks report were hashed but not opened for content; the flag digest was opened only to confirm that no flag is keyed to a drafting part 1 entry.
> My findings rest on the entries, the strategy, the device inventory, the mark layer, the language-zone file and the two witnesses, not on the set of automated checks's own checks.

> The grade of Daniel 2:5–13 depends on whether a entry's confidence must reflect its weaker edge. I read the grading rule that way because the entry before it is graded on the same edge.
> If a entry's grade is meant to describe its span as a whole, medium may stand for Daniel 2:5–13 and the fix would be a sentence weighing the onset edge instead.

> The parsing of the two forms in 1:16 as participles, and the count of the verb 'give' in chapter 1, come from the pointed text and a consonantal word match; no morphology layer is among my inputs.
> The durative reading of 1:16 and the three-movement support for the entries of chapter 1 are interpretive from the bytes, not read from the source from a parsed layer.

> Whether 1:17 belongs with 1:18-1:20 or closes the test episode is a class of question (a narrator's summary at a hinge) on which form evidence points one way but not strongly.
> It bears on the 1:16/1:17 seam, which no mark supports; medium is right and the final review may wish to see it.

> Whether a entry's grade follows its weaker edge. Daniel 2:17–19 has a well-supported onset and a close argued from one side; I read the grading rule as letting the weaker edge govern.
> If the grade is meant to describe the entry's unit rather than its edges, Daniel 2:17–19's medium may stand and only the both-sides weighing is owed.

> Whether entry prose may cite the strategy's rulings, guards and regions by letter. Five of the six entries do (all but Daniel 2:17–19, whose rejected alternative still cites one ruling label); the set of automated checks raised no flag on this part.
> If labels are not allowed in entries, the same low finding applies across the cluster and is a part-wide rewording, not six separate ones.

> Whether OSHB editorial notes and paseq owe disclosure in every entry whose span holds one. The mark layer's own note says the editorial notes are to be disclosed; the paseq layer is count-only. I raised the editorial notes at 2:29 and 2:31 and only mentioned the paseq at 2:23, 2:24 and 2:35.
> It decides whether Daniel 2:24–30 and Daniel 2:31–35 carry a defect or a courtesy gap, and whether three more entries owe a paseq mention.

> Whether the time phrase at 2:44 counts as an internal signal for the over-nine-verse exception. I read it as a link back to the kings of 2:37-2:43, not an onset.
> If it counts, Daniel 2:36–45 does not meet the exception as stated and a cut at 2:43/2:44 would have to be weighed in earnest.

> counted without a named script in the language and ketiv/qere annotations. I confirmed the facts by my own scans; I did not see the writers' scripts.
> The facts are true, but the evidence grade form the strategy asks for (a script with counted) is not met, and I cannot say whether the revision's fixed grammar allowed one.

> The two neighbouring tales tile their closing promotion notices differently: 2:49 sits inside a four-verse narrative entry (2:46-2:49, the context entry before this cluster), while 3:30 stands alone as a one-verse notice.
> Both are allowed by the book's rules and the difference has a textual ground (2:46-2:49 is narration throughout, while 3:28-3:29 is quoted speech), but a reader comparing tales may take it for inconsistency. It is a question for the final review, not a defect of either entry.

> Whether the set of automated checks's quotation check applies the same five-consecutive-words rule I was given; it reads GREEN with no flag while my test finds one run in Daniel 4:1–3.
> If the set of automated checks's rule is narrower, or exempts stock phrases, that part of the Daniel 4:1–3 finding falls away; the form part of the finding does not depend on it.

> Whether the unit type dialogue may cover a one-party address (Daniel 3:8–12).
> The closed vocabulary has no type for a single speech inside a tale. The entry's stated ground is inaccurate, but the choice between dialogue and narrative for 3:8-3:12 is a class question that touches other accusation and petition speeches in the book.

> Where the prescript belongs, closing the furnace tale or opening the first-person account, is left open by the plan; I judged the entries inside the parents as given.
> A different ruling would move the parent seam and with it Daniel 3:30 and Daniel 4:1–3.

> All readings run on one model family.
> Agreement between this lens and another is one family's voice, not independent confirmation.

> The four medium challenges are two seams, each seen from its two entries: the seam between the recital of the watcher's decree and the interpretation formula, and the seam after the narrator's one-verse notice.
> Counting them as four independent findings would overstate the disagreement with the entries; each seam needs one ruling that moves two entries.

> The book plan itself names the interpretation-formula verse as the turn inside Daniel's speech and lists the edge after the notice, with its PE, among the edges to weigh. My two seam challenges therefore also question how the plan's working notes are applied, on the ground of clause syntax read from the Aramaic line.
> A ruling for the entries as drawn can rest on the plan. The syntax reading (a dependent recital clause; a clause with no expressed subject) is my interpretive reading of single-witness bytes and was not checked against a grammar or a second witness.

> The verb echo between the notice and the interpretation formula is close-side evidence for reading the notice with what precedes it, and it agrees with the PE.
> It is the best case for keeping the notice apart from the fulfilment account; I weighed it as weaker than the missing subject of the following verse, and another reader may weigh it the other way.

> Whether the hyphenated device phrase in the dream-report entry counts as five consecutive WEB words depends on whether a hyphen is a word delimiter.
> If hyphens join words the observation falls away; I report it as a low secondary note, not a challenge.

> I did not read the content of the untyped editorial notes of the witness at the three verses where entries are silent on them; I know only their counts and that the layer labels them single-witness matter to disclose. Whether the entries owe that disclosure is not settled by anything I read.

> My run-of-five scan is my own reimplementation (case and punctuation ignored, whole book), not the campaign tool; the set of automated checks member web quotes was GREEN on entries in which I and the reconciling readings find unquoted runs.
> The tool gap adjudication round 6 recorded is still open; a green member is not evidence that rule a numbered rule holds.

> The root identity in Daniel 7:15–18 (7:19 word 3 with 7:16 word 6) and the sense of the duration phrase at oshb 4.16 were judged from the consonants and the WEB rendering, not from a morphology layer.
> Both are ordered under interpretive or under the WEB evidence grade for that reason.

> The seam at web 6:9/6:10 against 6:10/6:11, the role of 12:4, the appointed-time word at 11:27, 11:29 and 11:35, and the reach of rule a numbered rule are not ruled.
> They are divided readings or method questions for the final review; revision set 9 changes wording only.

> This pass’s context was compacted twice mid-run. The byte checks ran in batches before any ruling was written, the rulings were written after compaction from the work files and a summary, and a working file was written once at build time, not after each id.
> Entry quotations in the evidence outside the exact spans come from the earlier extraction and were not re-measured after compaction; every exact-span before text was re-measured as count 1.

> This pass ran on the model in the adjudicator role as a recorded a substitute model (an owner directive); the revision author, the editor measure and these rulings share one model family.
> Agreement among them is not independent confirmation; the rulings go to the final reviewer's end-of-campaign review (an owner directive).

> audit condition 1 to audit condition 6, audit condition 9 to audit condition 12 and audit condition 14 to audit condition 16 on the returned copy were not re-measured here, beyond the set of automated checks summary (GREEN, 82), the 26-place diff and the record counts.
> They rest on the editor own script; the pass 2 result is measured again in any case.

> The token 4:29 (English numbering) in Daniel 4:28 the observed signals, item 1 (counted from 0) produced no refs mirror key in my test. I infer the member does not read that field; I did not read its code.
> If a later set of automated checks version reads the field, a FAR SIDE key for that token would appear and would return here under audit condition 7.

> Why the universals member no longer flags the word only in Daniel 7:15–18 the stated reason for the boundary ('reading form only') on the returned copy was not established; I did not read the member's code.
> The triage count fell by one for a reason no one has stated from the code. It does not affect a ceiling, but the count 82 should not be read as a claim removed.

> The adjudication round 10 span on Daniel 11:21–28 the formula notes takes its words ('held low') from the grade statement of the same entry's the stated reason for the boundary and from confidence low; it is my wording, tested for flags and predicates but not reviewed by a blind reading yet.
> It is a place outside the 26 of adjudication round 9; the re-review must hold an item for it.

> Three pinned inputs were digest-verified but not opened for content: a working file, the reading plan for the book, the language-zone layer. adjudication round 3 was read for the grammar G and rulings a numbered adjudication item and a numbered adjudication item only; the log for lines 807-874 only.
> No ruling here rests on them; they are left out of inputs ruled on for that reason.

> The divided readings touched here are not ruled: the seam after web 6:9 or after web 6:10 (Daniel 6:4–9, Daniel 6:10–15), and whether the appointed-time word closes or opens at 11:27 and 11:29 (Daniel 11:21–28).
> They stand with the final reviewer's final review by adjudication round 9; the adjudication round 10 spans change no boundary, grade or unit type.

> Every role, both review readings and this ruling run on the model as a recorded a substitute model (an owner directive); one model family is one voice.

> The grade of the Daniel 6:10–15 finding is not resolved: adjudication round 9 let low stand for the same construction in Daniel 6:4–9 and the text reading reading graded medium; the reading's scale is not among my inputs.

> The candidate entries Daniel 5:5–9, Daniel 7:13–14 and Daniel 9:20–23 come from my search pattern scan and were not read in depth.

> The after text for Daniel 7:15–18 is my wording; no blind reading has tested it yet. An earlier wording with 'last verse' moved universals.claims seen from 89 to 90 with no flag change; the ordered wording leaves it at 89. I did not read the cause in the set of automated checks code.

> Two pinned inputs were digest-verified but not opened for content (the book strategy and the WEB/MT offset map) and are left out of inputs ruled on; several others were opened only in the ranges I needed.

> I did not re-measure audit condition 1 to audit condition 16 on a revision round file beyond the set of automated checks summary (GREEN, 82); I rely on a working file for them.

> The divided reading at web Dan 6:9 and 6:10 is not ruled.

> The first-deliverable bytes of a later re-reading readings and the continuation message are unavailable to me.

> Every role, both readings and this ruling run on the model as a recorded a substitute model (an owner directive).
> One model family is one voice; only the script outputs count as evidence, and the ruling is owed to the final reviewer's final review (an owner directive).

> The readings' grading scale is not among my inputs; I neither confirmed nor changed reading the text reading's grade of low.
> If the scale makes a refuted number medium, audit condition 13 on a revision round failed on that ground too; the order does not depend on it.

> Word numbers follow the whitespace words of the pinned OSHB file (no maqqef in the 7:14 line); no other tokenisation was tested.
> 'words 13 to 14 of 21' is true of this file's words only, as the entry's other word positions are.

> The sibling audit used my own search pattern for a device key followed by a word position (four places found); a position worded otherwise would be missed.
> It supports the reading of the entries' convention and is not a proof that no other device position in the 75 entries is wide.

> I opened adjudication round 1, adjudication round 2, adjudication round 3, adjudication round 7, adjudication round 9 and adjudication round 10 only in the parts I name in evidence, the measure only for its conditions, and did not open the book strategy beyond its digest (it is left out of inputs ruled on); the log only at lines 807 to 874.
> A condition of an earlier ruling outside those parts could bear on the restated audit conditions; audit condition 4, audit condition 5, audit condition 6, audit condition 8 and audit condition 10 are carried by reference, not re-read in their source rulings.

> I did not re-measure audit condition 1 to audit condition 16 on a revision round file beyond the set of automated checks summary (GREEN, 82) and the two-place diff; I rely on the pinned measure for the rest.
> The base of a revision round is taken as sound on the editor measure.

> My context was compacted once in this pass, after all measurements and before the deliverable was written. Quotations of earlier rulings, of the checkpoint evaluation and of the readings in evidence are from my working record of what the scripts printed, and where I mark a paraphrase they are not verbatim; every count and digest is from script output kept in work\.
> A reader should re-read the quoted source at the named path before relying on the exact wording of a quotation; the ordered span, the counts and the set of automated checks results do not depend on it.

> I ruled the three ids in one pass and wrote the progress file once, after all three, not after each; and the harness saved one oversized output of my first adjudication round 11 extract outside my OUT, which I did not open (I re-ran the script into a working file).
> A process deviation from the continuation clause of the instructions; no partial state was ever the deliverable.

> Whether oshb 7:14 closes the vision report, and the seam readings at oshb 6:11 and 6.12, are not ruled.
> They are divided or open readings and belong to the final reviewer's final review.

## 8. Licence and attribution

The Hebrew and Aramaic text is from the Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible, a transcription of the Westminster Leningrad Codex, released into the public domain by its transcribers; the morphological annotation is distributed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence and is attributed to the Open Scriptures project. The English text is the World English Bible, which is in the public domain. Quotations of either witness above carry these terms with them. This record makes no claim on either text beyond quotation for the purpose of showing what was argued from it.

A limit on the paragraph above. Those terms are stated here as the project's record for Ezekiel states them for the same two witnesses. Daniel's own files do not state them: a search of the Hebrew-Aramaic text file, the English text file, the section-mark layer, the formula inventory and the list accompanying the final entries for the words licence, public domain, Creative Commons or copyright found 0 occurrences. What Daniel's own files do say about their sources is quoted next. The licence terms should be confirmed against the witnesses' own distributions before this record is published.

> 6. Quotations are short and sliced by script, and they carry their attribution (OSHB/WLC; WEB). Never retype a

> untyped OSHB notes of the exact form KJV:Dan.c.v, keyed MT -> English; the numbering witness that web_mt_offset_map.json cross-checks

> non-variant, non-KJV OSHB notes (exegesis, alternative readings, punctuation divergences); single-witness, disclose. UNTYPED notes are captured and marked '(untyped)'.

> paseq (U+05C0) is a disjunctive stroke inside a verse. COUNT-ONLY: the extract drops segs, so an intra-verse POSITION claim is unsourceable from Dan_oshb.txt and must be read from the XML by exact path. Listed once per occurrence, so a verse may repeat.

> WLC (OSHB) - single witness; disclose on every citation

## 10. The apparatus's own words

Every sentence in this record that is not a quotation was assembled from one of the following strings. A mark such as %d or %s stands where a count or a value from the reports was inserted.

- # The division of Daniel into reading units: a record of what was disputed
- This record is generated mechanically from the reports of the readers who examined a proposed division of the book of Daniel into %d reading units. It is written for a reader of Daniel, not for a reader of the project that produced it: passages are named by chapter and verse, in the English numbering, with the Hebrew numbering added where the two differ.
- Every quotation set off with a rule at the left is a reader's own sentence, altered only by the mechanical substitutions listed in full near the end. Every other sentence is the generator's own frame, and every such sentence is printed in the last section so that the frame can be inspected apart from the evidence.
- This record makes no judgement of its own. It changes no unit, weighs no boundary and settles no dispute; it reports what the readers wrote. Its limits are stated in section 2 and are not small.
- ## 1. What made this book difficult
- Daniel is written in two languages. Of the %d units, %d lie in Hebrew, %d in Aramaic and %d cross from one to the other (%s). The formula inventory counts %s verses in %s chapters.
- The Hebrew and English traditions number the verses differently in four stretches, so that a boundary stated in one numbering can be misread in the other. The section-mark layer states the difference in these words:
- The Hebrew text carries paragraph marks, and the division had to decide how much weight each bears. The section-mark layer holds %d marked verses: %s.
- The book marks time with date notices and recurring formulae, and several of the disputes below turn on whether a formula opens a unit or merely continues one. The formula inventory records %s date notices and the following formulae:
- - “%s” (%s): %s occurrences
- The division as it stands is not confident. Its own grades of confidence are: %s. Its unit types are: %s.
- ## 2. How the division was examined, and what that does and does not establish
- The division was read in stages. Two first readings, here called reading A and reading B, each examined every unit without sight of the other (%d reports, %d findings). A reconciling reading then took both and said which stood (%d reports, %d findings). The entries were revised in rounds (%d revision logs opened here, with %d recorded changes), and the later revisions were re-read in pairs, one reading attending to scope and one to the text (%d reports). An audit followed (%d report and %d supplement). An adjudicator ruled between the stages (%d rounds, %d rulings).
- What this does not establish. Every reading at every stage was produced by one family of language model. Where two readings agree, that is one voice heard twice, not two independent witnesses, and agreement in this record must never be taken as confirmation. No human scholar has examined any unit. No reading consulted a version, a manuscript or a commentary beyond the two witnesses named in section 8. The readers said as much themselves; their own statements of limit are collected in section 6.
- Of the %d files the project lists as landed, %d were opened and quoted, %d were opened and checked but not quoted, and %d were not opened (%d closing messages and %d revision logs held outside the tree). Section 7 lists every one.
- ## 3. The disputes
- A passage appears here if either first reading challenged its entry, if the first readings differed, if a later re-reading challenged it or added a finding on it, or if the audit recorded a finding on it. %d of the %d units appear. They are ordered by the highest severity any reader assigned, then by their place in the book. Severity is the readers' own grade; most challenges concern how an entry words or supports its boundary, not where the boundary falls.
- By highest severity: %s.
